title: French high school students blockade hundreds of schools over conditions
seoTitle: France high school protests and blockades

tea.why: Students say classes are overcrowded, absent teachers are not replaced and school buildings are dilapidated and overheated.
tea.want: More teachers and staff, smaller classes, repaired buildings and more funding for public schools.
tea.changed: Oct 5: 413 schools disrupted, down from 564 on Friday; unions back a national day of protest on Oct 6.

summary: High school students in France have blockaded the entrances of hundreds of lycées since mid-September, protesting overcrowded classes, teacher shortages and run-down, overheated buildings. The movement started in the Paris region and spread nationwide; university students have joined in some cities. Some blockades turned into clashes with police, with bins and school buildings set on fire; the education minister said 24 schools had been burned or ransacked. The interior ministry says more than 5,000 people, mostly minors, have been arrested. The government says the grievances may be legitimate but the violence is not, and accuses hard-left politicians of encouraging it. Rights groups and families accuse police of excessive force: a 16-year-old in Tours lost sight in one eye and a 15-year-old in Lens lost a hand, the cause of which is under investigation. Unions back a national day of protest on October 6.
demands: Replace absent teachers and hire more staff
response: The government says the grievances may be legitimate but violence is not, blames hard-left politicians for stoking it, has closed 400–500 schools for safety and opened internal police probes into brutality allegations.

arrests.text: more than 5,000 arrested since Sept 28, mostly minors, according to the interior ministry

updates.text: A school entrance hall caught fire and pupils blocked trams; police opened probes into brutality claims against three pupils.
Clashes spread; several principals were injured, harassed or assaulted during blockades, authorities said.
About 400 schools closed; the education minister urged parents to keep children away from blockades.
The interior ministry put arrests above 5,000; about 735 establishments were affected on Friday.
A 15-year-old lost a hand outside a school in Lens; an investigation was opened into how it happened.
413 schools were disrupted, down from 564 on Friday; a national day of protest is set for Oct 6.
